messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED · service=serving-runtime severity=P1 · summary=illegal device address / misaligned access observed on multiple GPU nodes

oncall-lee: ack. I'm on it, switching to incident channel. tagging @sre-ana @runtime-raj · ETA 2m

sre-ana: grabbing logs from the first impacted node (gpu-node-17). seeing repeated: 
```
E CudaFailure: CUDA illegal memory access at 0x7f3b21c4d000
    at llama::kv_cache::read (kv_cache.cu:214)
    at serving::executor::run_step (executor.cc:342)
```
Also kernel dmesg: `nv 0000:01:00.0: pagewalk: misaligned address 0x7f3b21c4`

runtime-raj: thanks. is this correlated with the 03:52 deploy? @deploy-bot what rolled?

deploy-bot: rollout: serving-runtime:canary -> v3.2.7 at 2027-06-09T03:51:40Z by ci/pipeline #8421

oncall-lee: ok canary rolled 03:51. Node list shows 3 nodes with repeated container exits: gpu-node-17/19/23. Crashloop with SIGSEGV inside CUDA path.

infra-jun: I'm starting cordon+drain on gpu-node-17 to stop new pods landing, will keep one replica pinned for investigation (no full drain yet).

cs-emma: heads-up: we've already got one support ticket from a customer in us-west2 reporting 500 errors for embeddings endpoint. Putting them on priority alert and drafting a short status note.

runtime-raj: quick triage idea — this looks like a kernel-pagewalk misalignment that surfaces with our new allocator+prefetch path for quantized kernels. Can we temporarily disable the prefetch flag for the canary? Patch the config to set `SERVING_PREFETCH=0` for canary pods and restart just the canary replicas. That should avoid the misaligned walk while we investigate root cause.

oncall-lee: doing that now. Command: 
```bash
kubectl set env deploy/serving-runtime-canary SERVING_PREFETCH=0 -n serving-prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime-canary -n serving-prod
```

sre-ana: logs after the restart on node-19 show fewer illegal accesses immediately, but node-23 still fires about 1-2/min. Suspect a race that the prefetch toggle reduces but doesn't eliminate.

runtime-raj: good signal. plan B: scale down canary to 0 on affected AZ to prevent customer impact (we'll route to stable). I can trigger automatic fallback routing in the smart-router for requests hitting canary model variants.

infra-jun: cordon on node-23 completed; draining now. Migration shows one pod failed to resume on stable due to image pull timeout but that's unrelated — retrying.

cs-emma: customer update draft: "We observed a partial disruption to embeddings in us-west2. We mitigated by routing traffic away from impacted capacity; no data was lost. Engineering is continuing root cause analysis. ETA for full recovery: 60–90m." Thoughts? :warning:

oncall-lee: good. add that we rolled back the canary prefetch and are re-routing. say we will follow up with postmortem.

sre-ana: collecting core dumps from the affected containers and NVidia driver traces. attaching kernel logs snippet here: 
```
[ 1123.451234] nv: pagewalk: unaligned addr=0x7f3b21c4 len=64 ctx=0x0042
[ 1123.451239] nv: tlb_miss handler race, pid=7263 comm=serving-runtime
[ 1123.451244] GPU crash dump: GPU fault engine: illegal memory access (0x1)
```
This points to a race in pagewalk handling when multiple kernels concurrently access a mapping that hits a quantized memory region.

runtime-raj: noted. short-term mitigations logged: 
- Disable SERVING_PREFETCH on canary (done)
- Drain/cordon affected nodes (in progress)
- Route traffic to stable model variant and standby capacity (in progress)
- Increase per-pod eviction buffer (avoid restart storms)
Long-term: roll a patch to the allocator to align pagewalks or add serialization for hot paths; will schedule owner and ETA in postmortem.

oncall-lee: customers affected: 4 orgs reported errors, estimated request failure rate 8–14% for embeddings peak at 03:55–04:05 UTC. No billing anomalies detected.

cs-emma: sending the short notice now. I'll keep the ticket owners updated and offer traffic-splitting guidance for customers who need immediate mitigation.

sre-ana: capturing recording for postmortem. I'll stash the core dumps in s3://redwood-incident-dumps/6161717171/ and link in the postmortem.

runtime-raj: continuing investigation into race condition. ping me if any node shows repeat faults after re-routing — I want to capture perf counters.

oncall-lee: incident status: mitigated -> partial (traffic routed off canary, nodes cordoned, failures falling to <1% across region). Keeping channel open for final verification and PM notes. :thumbsup:
